notes.howTheyAreSet: What does not depend on the machine is held tight (the weight in KiB, the scripts, the number of requests, the layout shift): measured in the CI, with about 10 % of room, and each of them has caught or would have caught a real defect (the calendar made 141 requests). What depends on the machine is held loose (the performance score, the largest contentful paint, the blocking time): on the shared runners of the CI the same code gave a blocking time of 206 and then 480 ms on the dashboard (phone), 468, 712 and then 882 ms on the members page, so those limits are there to see a change of order of magnitude, not a difference of a few tens of percent. Each page is also run three times and the median run is judged.
notes.members: The page lists every member at once (300 in the QA dataset): on a phone, Lighthouse measured a blocking time from 420 to 880 ms and a performance score from 63 to 71, which is the cost of drawing and hydrating 300 rows, not a defect of the page. Paginating the list would lower it; that is a decision about the product, not about the measure.
